prompts.prompt: We want to automate the journeys in our E2E strategy (testing-quality-assurance/outputs/e2e-test-strategy.md) with Cypress. Cypress is not installed yet and the React app is in frontend/. Produce the implementation plan our two QA engineers will pick tasks from: a task breakdown with dependencies and effort, and a phased roadmap. Write it to cypress-implementation-plan.md. Work only from the files here, write the output file(s) named above, do not ask me any questions, and state any assumptions in the output.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill prescribes typed CYPRESS-NNN tasks (Setup/PageObject/CustomCommand/TestData/TestImplementation/Verification) with acceptance criteria, a Foundation -> P0 -> P1 -> P2 roadmap, data-cy selectors, and code only in an appendix. A model without it usually writes one task per journey and misses page objects, fixtures and the missing-UI dependencies.

floor_checks.text: Plan exists and links every journey E2E-001..E2E-004
floor_checks.check: test -f cypress-implementation-plan.md && for i in 1 2 3 4; do grep -q "E2E-00$i" cypress-implementation-plan.md || exit 1; done

rubric.criterion: Task structure follows the skill: CYPRESS-NNN IDs, a Type from the skill's set, Related Test, Dependencies, Estimated Effort, Acceptance Criteria
rubric.pass: At least 8 typed tasks covering Setup, PageObject, CustomCommand, TestData, TestImplementation and Verification, each with dependencies, effort and acceptance criteria
rubric.partial: Tasks present but missing types or acceptance criteria, or PageObject/CustomCommand/TestData tasks absent
rubric.fail: One coarse task per journey with no structure

rubric.criterion: Roadmap is phased Foundation first, then P0 (E2E-001, E2E-002), P1 (E2E-003), P2 (E2E-004)
rubric.pass: Phases in that order with tasks assigned to them and the critical path visible
rubric.partial: Phased but priorities mixed or Foundation not first

rubric.criterion: Grounded in the actual app and strategy
rubric.pass: Calls for data-cy attributes on LoginPage/BoardPage (they only have ids/classes) and flags that edit/complete/search/filter/bulk-select UI and test credentials/cleanup endpoint are missing as dependencies or risks
rubric.partial: Recommends data-cy but does not notice the missing UI or data gaps
rubric.fail: Generic plan that could apply to any app

rubric.criterion: Task breakdown is free of code; examples, if any, are in an appendix; no invented endpoints
rubric.pass: No code in tasks; any code in an Appendix; unknowns stated as assumptions
rubric.partial: A little code inline in tasks
rubric.fail: Plan is mostly code, or invents APIs/selectors as fact

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: could two engineers start tomorrow from this?

prompts.prompt: Release is Friday. Verify our Cypress suite against the E2E strategy and Cypress good practice: which journeys are implemented, what is missing, what is wrong in the specs, and whether this blocks release. Include a journey-to-spec traceability matrix. Write cypress-verification-report.md. Work only from the files here, write the output file(s) named above, do not ask me any questions, and state any assumptions in the output.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate makes P0 not implemented, hard-coded cy.wait and shared state between tests CRITICAL, and asks for findings ordered CRITICAL -> IMPORTANT -> SUGGESTION with a traceability matrix. A model without it tends to list issues flatly and may not call the release blocked, or may trust the plan's [x] checkboxes over the code.

floor_checks.text: Report flags the hard-coded waits by file
Report names the missing P0 journey

rubric.criterion: Planted spec defects found with location and impact
rubric.pass: cy.wait(5000)/cy.wait(3000) at login-create-task.cy.js lines 9/18, shared createdTitle and test 2 depending on test 1's login (no isolation), conditional modal test (lines 22-27), plus fragile selectors and should('exist') assertions
rubric.partial: Waits and one of isolation/conditional found, others missed
rubric.fail: Misses the hard waits or the isolation problem

rubric.pass: Matrix covers E2E-001..004: E2E-002 (P0) and E2E-004 have no spec; E2E-003 partial (repeated login, no page objects/commands/fixtures); notes the plan marks CYPRESS-006/008 done while the specs fail best practice
rubric.partial: Matrix present but misses that E2E-004 is missing or that E2E-003 is weak
rubric.fail: No matrix, or says all P0 journeys are covered

rubric.criterion: Severity follows the skill's gate and ordering
rubric.pass: P0 gap, hard waits and shared state are CRITICAL; missing page objects/custom commands IMPORTANT; ordered CRITICAL -> IMPORTANT -> SUGGESTION
rubric.partial: Severity labels used but some misassigned

rubric.criterion: Clear release call with what must change
rubric.pass: States release is blocked and lists the specific fixes to unblock (E2E-002 spec, replace waits with assertions/intercepts, isolate tests with beforeEach or cy.session)
rubric.partial: Hedged release call or fixes not tied to findings

rubric.pass: Does not claim the tests were run or that they pass/fail at runtime
rubric.fail: Fabricates run output or pass rates

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: the real CRITICAL defects with line numbers
traceability a release manager can read

prompts.prompt: Set up the Cypress foundation for this repo and implement the E2E-001 journey from the strategy: config, shared support code, test data, and the spec. Change the React components in frontend/src if needed for testability. Don't install packages or run Cypress; just write the files. Work only from the files here, write the output file(s) named above, do not ask me any questions, and state any assumptions in the output.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's patterns (data-cy selectors added to components, a cy.login custom command, page objects, fixture JSON test data, no hard-coded waits, isolated tests with cleanup) shape the code. Without it, a competent model often writes a single spec with id/class selectors, inline credentials and a cy.wait.

floor_checks.text: A spec exists and no numeric cy.wait is used
data-cy attributes added to components and used by the spec

rubric.pass: cypress.config.js with baseUrl, a cy.login custom command (cy.session acceptable), at least one page object, test data in cypress/fixtures/*.json
rubric.partial: Two or three of these present

rubric.criterion: E2E-001 spec is correct and isolated
rubric.pass: Setup in beforeEach or cy.session, creates a task and asserts the exact title appears in the To do column, cleans up the created task (via API, with the endpoint stated as an assumption)
rubric.partial: Works but no cleanup or asserts only existence
rubric.fail: Depends on test order, uses hard waits, or does not assert the title

rubric.criterion: Component changes are minimal and testability-focused
rubric.pass: Adds data-cy to LoginPage/BoardPage inputs, buttons, columns and cards without changing behaviour
rubric.partial: Adds data-cy but also unrelated refactors

rubric.pass: Unknowns (credentials source, delete endpoint) are env/fixture-driven and stated as assumptions
rubric.partial: One hard-coded guess without a note
rubric.fail: Hard-coded secrets or invented APIs presented as real

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: would the spec be stable in CI?
